findings.title: Days with a date override skip the busy-time check
findings.body:
When a slot falls inside a date override, `dateOverrideExist` is true and line 133 returns `true`. That return happens before `busy.every(...)` at line 153. So a fixed or loose host with an override on a given day is shown as free for every slot in the override window, even if a booking or calendar event overlaps it.

`checkIfIsAvailable` is called with `...schedule` at lines 488-493 and 513-518. `schedule` carries both `dateOverrides` and `busy`, so the early return skips the host's real busy times. The user sees no error. Overbooked slots are offered, and the conflict only surfaces at booking time, if it surfaces at all.

The new test only has an override and no busy time, so it does not catch this.

Fix: do not return early. Use the override result only to decide whether to skip the working-hours check, then fall through to the busy loop.

findings.title: Working-hours check rejects slots when a host has more than one working-hour entry on a day
findings.body:
`workingHours.find(...)` returns true, meaning "outside working hours", as soon as any entry that includes the day does not contain the slot. It does not check whether some entry contains it.

A host has more than one entry for the same weekday in several common cases:
- split availability, such as 09–12 and 13–17;
- schedules that `getWorkingHours` splits when they overflow into the neighbouring day (`packages/lib/availability.ts:103-121`). That happens for organizers far from UTC, such as an NZ-based host.

A 10:00 slot is inside 09–12 but outside 13–17. The 13–17 entry makes `find` return true, so the slot is dropped. All slots on those days can vanish, and `getSlots` had already produced them correctly.

Separately, line 142 sets `end` to the same expression as `start` (`slotStartTime`), so `end > workingHour.endTime` never checks the slot end. A slot starting at 16:30 with a 60-minute event passes a 09–17 window.

Fix: compute `end` from `slotEndTime`. Reject only when no entry for that day contains `[start, end]`, using `workingHours.some(...)` for containment. Then add a test with a split schedule.

findings.title: Dead identity comparison and server-local date formatting in the override check
findings.body:
Line 114 compares two new `Dayjs` objects with `===`, which is always false. The `return true` on line 115 is dead code. The "zero-length override" case only works by accident, through the `isAfter(end)` check at line 123.

Line 110 formats `dayjs(date.start)`, which is in server-local time. It is compared with the UTC-formatted `slotStartTime` on line 111. The result depends on the server's `TZ`. Use `dayjs.utc(date.start)`.

The override's start and end are also compared in UTC, so a late-evening override in a far-away organizer timezone can cross the UTC date boundary. Its slots on the next UTC day then miss the `dateOverrideExist` match.

findings.title: Timezone shift of overrides can wrap past midnight and drop the override
findings.body:
`offset` can be large, such as +15h for a UTC-5 organizer and a UTC+10 invitee. Lines 219-223 reduce `hour()*60 + minute()` modulo 24h and do not carry the day. An override of 09:00–17:00 can become start 00:00 and end 08:00 on the wrong invitee day.

If only one end wraps, `endTime < startTime`. `buildSlots` then skips the range through `if (start >= end) continue` (line 68), and the override's slots silently vanish.

The `activeOverrides` filter at line 206 still matches the unshifted pseudo-UTC `override.start` against the invitee's day boundaries.

The new test only covers +5:30 vs +6:00, which never wraps. Consider either clamping or splitting at the day boundary, or at least adding a test with a distant timezone.

Minor: `dayjs(override.start.toString())` on lines 212-213 round-trips through a locale-dependent string and drops milliseconds. `dayjs(override.start)` is enough. When `override.timeZone` is undefined, `.tz(undefined)` silently falls back to the default timezone. The field is optional in `packages/types/schedule.d.ts`.

findings.title: New test covers one timezone pair and none of the new availability checks
findings.body:
The new `getSchedule` call uses the +5:30 day window (`T18:30:00.000Z` to `T18:29:59.999Z`) with a +6:00 invitee. The +6:00 day starts at 18:00Z, so the window does not match the timezone it claims to test. It also only exercises a 30-minute offset that cannot wrap.

No test covers the new working-hours check in `checkIfIsAvailable`. A split schedule (two ranges per day) would show the bug in the working-hours finding. No test has a date override and an existing booking on the same day, which would show the missing busy check. No test covers a round-robin or collective host with an override, although the PR title is about that scenario.

contracts.action: checkIfIsAvailable now evaluates date overrides and working hours for each fixed and loose host before the busy check
contracts.equivalent_path: Previously only `busy` and `currentSeats` were evaluated here. Overrides and working hours were applied only in `getSlots` (`packages/lib/slots.ts:206-246`), where slots are generated.
contracts.before_after: Before: the function checked currentSeats, then busy times. After: it checks currentSeats, then override and working-hours membership. When an override matches it returns true and skips the busy loop (lines 133-135). The busy loop at line 153 is reached only when no override applies to the slot's UTC date.
contracts.visible_effect: The booker's slot list. Slots on days with an override ignore existing bookings and calendar busy times. Hosts with multiple ranges per day lose slots.
contracts.failure_mode: No error is raised. Wrong slots are shown silently: overlapping slots are offered, or valid slots are removed.

contracts.action: getUserAvailability's per-user timeZone is attached to each date override and used to shift override times into the invitee's timezone
contracts.equivalent_path: Working hours are converted from UTC minutes to invitee-local time via `getWorkingHours({ utcOffset })` (packages/lib/slots.ts:170-176). Overrides were previously read as raw UTC hours and minutes.
contracts.before_after: Before: override.start/end UTC hour and minute were used directly. After: they are shifted by (inviteeOffset - organizerOffset). The result is correct without wrapping, but wraps past midnight are not handled.
contracts.visible_effect: Override slots shown to invitees in a timezone different from the organizer's.
contracts.failure_mode: If the shift wraps a day, or only one end wraps, the override range is dropped or lands on the wrong day. This is silent.

summary:
I found one blocker and one fix in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts`, plus three smaller items. I only read the code; nothing was built or run.

- **Blocker, line 133:** when a slot falls inside a date override, `checkIfIsAvailable` returns `true` before the busy-time loop. Bookings and calendar events are then ignored on any day with an override, so overlapping slots are offered with no error.
- **Fix, line 138:** the new working-hours check treats a slot as outside hours if any one of the host's entries for that day fails to contain it. Hosts with split ranges, or with schedules that overflow into the next day, lose valid slots. The `end` value on line 142 is also computed from the slot start, so the slot's end is never checked.
- **Consider:** the override check has dead code and server-local date formatting (`slots.ts` lines 110-114).
- **Consider:** the timezone shift of overrides in `packages/lib/slots.ts` can wrap past midnight and drop the override.
- **Consider:** the new test only covers a +6:00 invitee, using a +5:30 day window. It does not cover split schedules or an override on a day with an existing booking.

`packages/types/schedule.d.ts` only adds an optional `timeZone` field, and I found nothing to flag in it.
